evidence: CreateProjectUseCase.ts, CreateTaskUseCase.ts and CreateUserUseCase.ts each contain `Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 11)`, so the ID-generation policy is written out three times.

AssignTaskUseCase.execute, CreateTaskUseCase.execute, MarkTaskDoneUseCase.execute and ListTasksUseCase.execute each map a task to `{ id, projectId, title, description, dueDate, status, assignedToUserId }` by hand.
dtos.ts declares CreateTaskResponse, AssignTaskResponse and MarkTaskDoneResponse with identical fields and repeats the same shape inline in ListTasksResponse.tasks.
ListTasksUseCase.execute uses taskRepository.findByProjectIdAndStatus and findByProjectIdAndAssignee for single filters but falls back to `tasks.filter(...)` in memory when both filters are set.
CreateUserUseCase builds `const user: User = { id, name }` as a plain object, while CreateProjectUseCase uses `new ProjectEntity(...)` and CreateTaskUseCase uses `new TaskEntity(...)`.
CreateTaskUseCase passes the literal 'todo' as the initial status, so the default-status rule sits in the application layer rather than in TaskEntity.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module has one concern: its files are application use cases plus their DTOs, all about project, task and user management. It still fails the rubric because several rules are copied into multiple files instead of living in one place:
(1) ID generation. The same `Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 11)` line appears in three use cases.
(2) Task-to-DTO mapping. The same seven-field object literal is built in four use cases.
(3) Task response shape. dtos.ts declares the same seven-field structure four separate times.
(4) Initial task status. CreateTaskUseCase hardcodes 'todo' itself rather than leaving that default to the TaskEntity abstraction.

The use cases also don't use the module's abstractions consistently. ListTasksUseCase uses repository queries for single filters but filters in memory when both filters are set. CreateUserUseCase builds a plain `User` object literal, while the project and task use cases build entity classes.
